articles.title: He left 28 years ago, now after 36,000 miles Karl Bushby is almost home
articles.summary: Global walker Karl Bushby is almost within sight of his journey's end after 28 years away.
articles.content:
With his journey almost complete, Karl Bushby reflects on adventures that have taken him across four continents, as well as strained relationships and how life as he knows it is about to change dramatically.

Back in 1998, the former paratrooper, then aged 29, set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, to walk an unbroken path to his home city of Hull, without breaking two self-imposed rules: not to return to the UK until he had completed his journey, and not to use transport to advance.

Now 57, he is embarking on his final few miles having hacked his way through the jungles of the Darién Gap, crossed the frozen Bering Strait and, just a few weeks ago, swum the English Channel.

At the end, he will be met by his 36-year-old son Adam, a 12-year-old granddaughter whom he has never met, his father and brothers. His mother will be waiting at his childhood home that he left 28 years ago.

articles.personality_title: Karl Bushby nears end of 28-year, 36,000-mile walk home
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In 1998, Karl Bushby, a former soldier, began a unique journey to walk from Chile back to his hometown in the UK without using any transport. He planned to complete this long walk without returning home until the journey was finished.

**What happened** – After 28 years and 36,000 miles on foot, Karl is now close to finishing his trip. He has walked through jungles, crossed icy waters, and even swum across the English Channel. He started his walk at age 29 and is now 57, preparing to take his last steps home.

**Impact** – Karl’s journey shows incredible determination and strength. Walking such a long distance without shortcuts is very rare. It also highlights the emotional side, as he will finally meet family members he has not seen in decades, including his son and granddaughter.

**What's next step** – Karl will soon arrive in his hometown of Hull, where his family will welcome him. This moment marks the end of his long adventure and the start of a new chapter with his loved ones.

**One-sentence takeaway** – After nearly three decades walking 36,000 miles, Karl Bushby is about to complete an extraordinary journey back home.

articles.personality_title_es: Karl Bushby se acerca al final de su caminata de 28 años y 36,000 millas hacia casa
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En 1998, Karl Bushby, un exsoldado, comenzó un viaje único caminando desde Chile hasta su ciudad natal en el Reino Unido, sin usar transporte. Planeó no regresar a casa hasta terminar su viaje.

**Qué pasó** – Después de 28 años y 36,000 millas a pie, Karl está cerca de terminar su recorrido. Ha cruzado selvas, aguas congeladas e incluso nadó el Canal de la Mancha. Comenzó su caminata a los 29 años y ahora tiene 57, preparándose para sus últimos pasos hacia casa.

**Impacto** – El viaje de Karl muestra una gran determinación y fuerza. Caminar una distancia tan larga sin atajos es muy raro. También destaca el lado emocional, ya que finalmente se encontrará con familiares que no ha visto en décadas, incluyendo a su hijo y nieta.

**Próximo paso** – Karl pronto llegará a su ciudad natal, Hull, donde su familia lo recibirá. Este momento marcará el final de su larga aventura y el comienzo de una nueva etapa con sus seres queridos.

**Resumen en una frase** – Después de casi tres décadas caminando 36,000 millas, Karl Bushby está a punto de completar un viaje extraordinario de regreso a casa.
